concepts.title: Function components
concepts.summary: A component is a function that takes props and returns what should be on the screen.
misconceptions: A component is an object with methods, like a class.

concepts.title: State
concepts.summary: State is a value a component remembers between renders, and changing it is what asks React to run the component again.
misconceptions: A plain variable in the component body would work just as well.

concepts.title: What a render actually is
concepts.summary: A render is React calling your function to find out what the screen should look like — it is not the browser painting.
misconceptions: A render means the DOM was updated.

concepts.title: What a hook is
concepts.summary: A hook is a function that lets a component use React features, and it must be called in the same order on every render.
misconceptions: Hooks can be called conditionally as long as the condition is stable.

concepts.title: What triggers a re-render
concepts.summary: A component re-renders when its own state changes or when its parent re-renders, and then its effects run.
misconceptions: A component only re-renders when its own state changes.

concepts.title: useState
concepts.summary: useState returns the current value and a setter, and calling the setter schedules a re-render with the new value.
misconceptions: The setter changes the variable you already have in scope.

concepts.title: State updates do not apply immediately
concepts.summary: After you call the setter the variable you are holding still has the old value — the new one arrives on the next render.
misconceptions: setCount(count + 1) updates count, so I can read it on the next line.
Calling the setter twice in a row adds two.

concepts.title: Why you replace state instead of changing it
concepts.summary: React decides whether to re-render by comparing the old value to the new one, so editing the old object in place looks like nothing happened.
misconceptions: Pushing onto the array and calling the setter with it is the same as passing a new array.

concepts.title: useEffect
concepts.summary: useEffect runs a piece of code after the render that it belongs to, for work that is not part of producing the screen.
misconceptions: useEffect runs before the component renders, like a constructor.

concepts.title: The dependency array
concepts.summary: The array says which values the effect reads, and React re-runs the effect whenever one of them differs from last time.
misconceptions: The dependency array is a list of things I want the effect to change.
An empty array just means run it once, so it is the safe default.

concepts.title: Stale values in effects and handlers
concepts.summary: A function created during one render keeps that render's values forever, so an effect with a missing dependency reads an old one.
misconceptions: Reading count inside the callback gives me whatever count is now.
If the value is wrong I should move the variable outside the component.

concepts.title: Effect cleanup
concepts.summary: Returning a function from an effect tells React how to undo it, and React runs that before the effect goes again and when the component leaves.
misconceptions: Cleanup only runs when the component is removed from the screen.

concepts.title: When effects run
concepts.summary: React finishes the render and lets the browser paint, then runs your effects — so the user sees the first frame before the effect has happened.
misconceptions: The effect runs before the user can see anything, so a flash is impossible.

concepts.title: useRef
concepts.summary: A ref is a box that survives re-renders and does not cause one when you change it, which is what makes it different from state.
misconceptions: Changing a ref re-renders the component, like state does.

concepts.title: useMemo and useCallback
concepts.summary: Both skip work when their dependencies have not changed — useMemo keeps a value, useCallback keeps a function.
misconceptions: Wrapping everything in useMemo makes the app faster.

concepts.title: Custom hooks
concepts.summary: A custom hook is a function starting with `use` that calls other hooks, so shared logic moves without the state being shared.
misconceptions: Two components using the same custom hook share its state.
